t: Bavaria was a duchy from c. 555 to 1623, ruled in turn by the Agilolfings, Frankish kings, Luitpoldings, Welfs and Wittelsbachs.
Bavarian settlers and the church of Salzburg spread Christianity and German speech into the eastern Alps and Austria.
Under Maximilian I it led the Catholic League and in 1623 was raised to an electorate, later the Kingdom of Bavaria.
dyk: Austria began as an eastern frontier march of Bavaria and only became a separate duchy in 1156; Bavarian dialects are still spoken across most of Austria.
ev: The Franks recognise Garibald I of the Agilolfing family as duke of the Bavarians
Boniface organises the bishoprics of Salzburg, Regensburg, Freising and Passau
Charlemagne deposes Duke Tassilo III, ending Agilolfing rule
The Privilegium Minus separates Austria from Bavaria as a duchy
Frederick Barbarossa grants Bavaria to Otto of Wittelsbach
Emperor Louis IV reunites Upper and Lower Bavaria
The Landshut War of Succession ends; Albert IV reunites Bavaria
Maximilian I receives the electoral dignity; Bavaria becomes an electorate

f.capital: Regensburg; later Munich (with Landshut, Ingolstadt and Straubing during partitions)
f.predecessor: Kingdom of the Franks; Roman provinces of Raetia and Noricum
